subject.title: Feature: enrich usage/status JSON with agent, cron, and channel labels

question: Should OpenClaw promote the existing partial status/sessions-usage metadata into a stable JSON attribution contract, and what privacy policy should channel target identity follow?
rationale: The requested fields widen official machine-readable telemetry surfaces and may expose channel routing details, so the schema and privacy semantics need maintainer intent before automation implements them.

options.title: Define a narrow stable attribution contract
options.body: Add optional agent/session/cron/channel/model/runtime fields with raw channel target IDs omitted by default and documented as the canonical JSON shape.

options.title: Defer until broader observability design
options.body: Keep this open as product input and avoid piecemeal JSON fields until status, usage, telemetry export, and privacy policy are designed together.

options.title: Fold only the friendly-label subset into the status-label issue
options.body: Leave this issue open for the broader JSON export while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/51184 handles CLI/TUI display labels only.

recommendation.title: Define a narrow stable attribution contract
recommendation.body: Add optional agent/session/cron/channel/model/runtime fields with raw channel target IDs omitted by default and documented as the canonical JSON shape.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans provider usage, status JSON, and privacy/product policy rather than only one implementation file.
